q1.explanationZh: 爸爸看了女孩手肘上的伤口，说会好起来的，女孩说手肘没有以前那么疼了（It doesn’t hurt as much as it did）。B 错：膝盖还是很疼；C 错：脚踝走路时还很痛，要去看医生。

q2.explanationZh: 男孩的爸爸要加班，不能开车送他们；主路在施工，今天没有公交车经过电影院，所以女孩说只能坐火车了（The train’s our only option, then）。B 错：公交站只是顺路去看明天上学的公交信息；C 错：女孩妈妈的车坏了。

q3.explanationZh: 这个周末网球场有比赛，所以志愿者要到湖边放船的地方集合（where the boats are kept, by the lake）。C 错：网球场是最近的集合点，但这周末不能用；A 错：大门人太多，他们想找个安静的地方。

q4.explanationZh: 家里的面包吃完了，妈妈让他吃一块昨晚剩下的披萨，男孩笑着说只好这样了（it looks like I’ll have to!）。A 错：他想吃三明治，但没有面包了；C 错：香肠和鸡蛋要留到晚上吃。

q5.explanationZh: 女孩说那些蹦来蹦去的小袋鼠很好玩，说明他们看到了袋鼠。C 错：老虎在室内，他们没看到；B 错：长颈鹿宝宝太小，还不让游客看，要以后再去看。

q6.explanationZh: 男孩说新买的夹克太紧了（this jacket’s far too tight），而且标签已经剪了，不能退。B 错：夹克里面只能穿 T 恤，T 恤本身没问题；A 错：他只是想穿运动衫，但穿不进夹克里。

q7.explanationZh: 男孩说他们觉得不在咖啡馆吃饭，而是大家一起在户外做饭会更有意思，也就是在户外烧烤庆祝生日。B、C 错：骑车去海边、玩球是他们以后的计划。

q8.explanationZh: 男孩说这节课有些任务很有挑战性，要花一阵子才能做出答案；女孩也说问题开始以为很简单，后来变得难多了——两人都认为老师给的任务有难度。B 错：男孩说逼自己一把就能做得更好，但这不是老师激励的结果，女孩也没有同意；C 错：男孩在别的课上已经玩过这种游戏，并不新颖。

q9.explanationZh: 广场不让玩滑板了，男孩说只能另找地方，还希望能像别的城镇那样建一个滑板公园——他是在抱怨能玩滑板的地方太少。A 错：他没有提醒朋友哪里不能去；C 错：人行道只是“还行”，他没有建议去一个新地方。

q10.explanationZh: 男孩说他以前从没演过主角（a lead role），得到这个角色时他非常为自己骄傲（I was so pleased with myself）。B 错：大家说他演得好，但他没有提到剧评；C 错：他帮忙写了一些台词，但不确定写得好不好。

q11.explanationZh: 男孩说奶酪洋葱派和沙拉很好吃，女孩说就冲这一点她一定会再去（I’d definitely go again for that reason!）——两人都认为食物好吃。B 错：女孩觉得服务员很有趣，男孩却不这么认为；C 错：男孩觉得椅子太硬，女孩没注意。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩本以为今天会犯很多错，所以很高兴自己没有出错（I’m glad I didn’t），也就是松了一口气。A 错：差点扭伤脚踝的是女孩；C 错：他对表现并不失望，还希望下次更容易。

q13.explanationZh: 女孩说她睡得很好，这里不像上次住的营地那样吵（there isn’t loads of noise），说明她觉得这里很安静。B 错：她提到有两个游泳池和排球场，并没有说设施少；C 错：营地离海边要走挺远，位置并不方便。

q14.explanationZh: 八点要在校门口集合，八点一刻（quarter past eight）出发。8:30 是平时的上学时间，8:00 是集合时间，都不是出发时间。

q15.explanationZh: 老师说这次参观重点是北极地区，特别是那里的海洋生物（the sea creatures there）。北极也有陆地动物，但不是这次的重点。

q16.explanationZh: 老师让学生仔细阅读展品介绍，选出最有趣的一件来画一幅画（make a drawing）。这次不做小测验（quiz），也不能用手机拍照。

q17.explanationZh: 天气预报说明天天气好，所以大家去湖边（the lake）吃野餐。博物馆旁边的花园只是可以散步的地方，咖啡馆也不去。

q18.explanationZh: 参观结束后，老师要学生写一篇报告（write a report），不用做演讲（presentation）。

q19.explanationZh: 教授的姓是 Hawthorpe，录音中逐个字母拼出 H-A-W-T-H-O-R-P-E，注意拼写。

q20.explanationZh: Joe 说开帆船环游希腊群岛、在各个港口停靠听起来太棒了，他迫不及待——他对要去的不同地方感到兴奋。A 错：他说开帆船并不是他的梦想；B 错：他不知道自己能不能学会。

q21.explanationZh: 妈妈说至少要能认出并记住船上各个部分的名称，比如船头船尾的专门说法。B 错：他们没有计划观光；C 错：开帆船不需要特别强壮，所以没去健身房。

q22.explanationZh: Joe 说他没想到只用这么短的时间就能学会开帆船（in such a short time），比他想的简单。A 错：他们是和其他家庭、教练一起结队航行的，并不是单独航行很远；C 错：教练在附近让他觉得安全，但这不是让他惊讶的事。

q23.explanationZh: 进港时要很小心，否则会撞坏船，Joe 说他每次都做得很好（I got that right every time）。A 错：他只是说没撞到东西，保持方向却做得不好；C 错：海图是爸妈负责看的。

q24.explanationZh: 闪电照亮天空时，Joe 不敢相信景色的变化，颜色非常美（the colours were gorgeous），他感到惊叹。B 错：他们当时不在海上，看到船被风吹得摇来摇去他觉得很不可思议，不是害怕；C 错：暴风雨持续了好几个小时。

q25.explanationZh: Joe 说上岸后吃到了各种好吃的东西，很多以前都没听说过，他很喜欢（I really enjoyed that）。A 错：他原以为上岸能去跑步，但没时间；B 错：他想和当地人聊天，但希腊语不够用。

content.v: Test Four. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now open your question papers and look at Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. What does the girl say feels better today?
How’s your knee today after falling off your skateboard yesterday?
It’s still sore, Dad. But it wasn’t a very serious fall.
I know. Let’s have a look at that cut on your elbow… Well, it looks like it’s going to be OK.
It doesn’t hurt as much as it did.
That cream you put on it has done its job. How about your ankle?
It still feels painful when I try to walk.
I’m sure it isn’t broken but let’s make an appointment for a check at the doctor’s anyway.
Two. How will they get to the cinema?
Do you still want to go to the cinema later?
Yeah – do you think your dad’ll give us a lift? My mum’s car’s broken down.
Well, usually that’d be fine – he’s working late this evening, though. There aren’t any buses going past the cinema today because they’re doing some work on the main road.
The train’s our only option, then. Shall we walk to the station together about half five?
Sure. On our way past we can see if there’s any information at the bus stop about buses to school tomorrow.
Three. Where should the volunteers meet?

Want to see a cleaner, greener town park? If so, join us for the monthly litter pick-up. Recently our group changed its meeting point to the front of the tennis court, but we won’t be able to meet there this weekend as there’s an important match on. Instead, we’re asking you to come along to where the boats are kept, by the lake. A lot of park visitors come and go through the main gate, so we’d prefer a quieter place where volunteers will find each other more easily.
Four. What’s the boy having for lunch?
I’m off to volleyball practice soon, Mum.
You’ll need some lunch before you go. What about a sandwich? Or there’re some sausages and eggs in the fridge.
Just a sandwich please. I’m in a hurry.
Oh dear, I forgot. We’ve run out of bread. You had the last slice earlier. But you can have a piece of last night’s pizza.
(laughing)
Oh well, it looks like I’ll have to!
Sorry! But don’t worry, I’m going shopping later so I’ll get more bread. And this evening we can have sausage and eggs.
Five. What did they see at the wildlife park yesterday?
It was a great trip to the wildlife park yesterday, wasn’t it?
Yeah – a shame not to see the tigers, though. I love watching them.

Yeah, I know, they were inside – probably sleeping after lunch! But those little kangaroos, jumping about all over the place were funny. And the guide said there’s a new baby giraffe. It’s kept away from the public for now cos it’s so small. We’ll have to go back and see it once it’s old enough to come outside.
I know – it sounds really cute.
Yeah!
Six. What does the boy have a problem with at the moment?
Oo-oh, you’re looking very nice and stylish today!

Thanks – Mum and I went out on a shopping trip yesterday and I got all this new stuff. I think this jacket’s far too tight. It’s a shame it’s too late to take it back cos I’ve taken the label off and I’m wearing it. I can only wear a T-shirt under it, and I really wanted to wear a sweatshirt today as I think it’s going to be cold later!
That’s what I heard.
Seven. How did the boy celebrate his birthday?

Hi Grandma, thanks so much for my birthday present! I had a great day with Mum and Dad, and several of my friends came along. We thought it would be more fun if, rather than eating in the café, we all cooked everything outside. And my friends put their money together and got me a bike helmet – remember mine was too small? We’ve already planned to cycle to the beach. Hopefully the weather’ll be good and we can play ball! OK, well, thanks again and I’ll see you soon!
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear two students talking about their English literature lesson.
I’ve never played a game like that in an English literature class before.

Haven’t you? I’ve done it a few times in other classes. Some of the tasks we had to do in this lesson were challenging though… it took me a while to get the answers. Some of the classmates said the same.
I thought the questions would be easy when we started but they got much harder actually.
Still, one thing I learned in that lesson is that if I push myself, I can do better.
Well, I know I could achieve more if I tried.
Nine. You will hear two friends talking about skateboarding in their town.
I like what they’ve done to the town square with the trees and everything. It looks nicer but it’s a pity we aren’t allowed to skateboard there anymore.
I know, but it’s safer for pedestrians.
We’ll have to find somewhere else to go. I wish they’d build a skateboard park for us like they’ve got in other towns.
Maybe we should ask for one!
I’m not sure who to ask about it, but yeah, maybe. The pavements here are OK for skateboarding on, but it’d be better if they were smoother.
I know.
Ten. You will hear a boy talking to a friend about a play he acted in.
Was it last night that you were in that play at the theatre?
Yes – didn’t you come to see the opening night? I’ve never been in a lead role before. I couldn’t believe it when they gave it to me – I was so pleased with myself.
Well, you’ve worked really hard on your acting skills. You deserve it!
Oh, thanks! Actually, I was a bit nervous, too. I helped with the lines for some of the main scenes. I’m not sure how brilliant they were though.
Look, everyone said you acted well, so just enjoy the experience!
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about a café they’ve been to.
That was kind of your mum, taking us to that café for lunch.
Yes – it opened last week. I expected them to serve the usual café stuff – but those cheese and onion pies and salads were delicious.
I’d definitely go again for that reason! Our order took a while to arrive, but at least the waiter made us laugh.
If you found it funny… Can’t say I did. It was nice there – but the chairs were a bit hard. I prefer places with sofas and stuff.
Oh, I didn’t really notice.
Maybe it was just me!
Twelve. You will hear two friends talking about an outdoor rock-climbing lesson.
What an incredible experience!
I know. I was so scared looking down.
Yeah, even though we weren’t at the top … actually, I used to be quite afraid of heights. I was sure I’d get loads of things wrong today so I’m glad I didn’t … I’d worried about that a bit. And
you
nearly injured your ankle! I’m hoping it’ll be easier next time.
Mmm. I think that today was enough for me. I feel the next lesson could be just too challenging.
Isn’t that a bit negative? And after today, who knows how good we might get at it.
Thirteen. You will hear a brother and sister talking about a campsite.
It’s soooo great to be on holiday here with Mum and Dad. What do you think of the campsite?

I like it. I thought it’d be nearer the sea – it’s quite a walk – but otherwise it’s an OK choice. It’s good there are two pools so the little kids can play around in one and the older kids like us can swim in the other, and at least there’s a volleyball court. Anyway, I’ve slept really well – there isn’t loads of noise like at that other campsite we stayed in – remember those guys with guitars?
Yeah, I liked listening to them, though!
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a teacher giving her class some information about a trip to a museum.
OK, everyone, I’d like to tell you a bit about our class trip to the Natural History Museum tomorrow.
We need to leave a little earlier than our usual school start time of eight thirty, so please make sure you’re ready and waiting at the school gate by eight, ready to set off at quarter past eight.

There are loads of interesting things to see at the museum. Our visit will focus on the Arctic region of the world – in particular, the sea creatures there. There are land animals, too, but because we’re studying the oceans in class at the moment, we’ll concentrate on that.

You’ll have a great time looking at all the displays, but there’s work to do, too! Not a quiz this time – I’d like you to read the display information carefully and choose the most interesting item to make a drawing of. I know you’d probably like to take a photo or two but no mobile phones, please.

So, about lunchtime… The museum has a café, but the school kitchen will provide a packed lunch for everyone, including sandwiches, fruit and water. There’s a lovely garden to walk around in beside the museum. The weather forecast is good for tomorrow, so we’ll go down to the lake and have our picnic there.

We’ll see more of the museum in the afternoon. Make notes because after our visit, I’m going to ask you to write a report about it. Don’t worry – you won’t have to do a presentation, you’ll be pleased to hear!
Before we go, I’d like you to look at some research by a famous professor, Helen Hawthorpe. I’ll just spell her surname for you and you can look her up on the internet. It’s H-A-W-T-H-O-R-P-E.
Any questions?
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a boy called Joe Wilson, who is talking about a sailing holiday he went on with his parents.
In the holiday programme today I’m talking to Joe Wilson who’s just been on a sailing holiday with his parents. How did you first feel about this idea, Joe?

When Dad asked me whether I fancied it I said yes immediately. I wouldn’t say going sailing was a dream of mine and I didn’t know whether I’d be able to do it, but sailing round the Greek islands stopping at all the harbours sounded brilliant and I couldn’t wait.
Before your holiday did you do anything to prepare for going on a sailing boat?

Mum said we should at least be able to identify and remember the names of all its different bits – the special words for the front and back and stuff. We didn’t plan sightseeing cos we weren’t sure we’d have time. You don’t need to be especially strong for sailing, so there was no need to start going to the gym or anything.
How was the training?

It lasted a week. I hadn’t realised you could become a sailor in such a short time – it was less complicated than I’d expected. In the second week, we managed our own boat. We stayed in a group, with other families on their boats and the instructors on theirs – it made me feel safer going round the islands with them nearby!
What were you best at when sailing?

When you arrive at a harbour, you have to be careful, otherwise you could damage the boat. I got that right every time, though I can’t say the same for keeping the boat going in the right direction. I didn’t crash into anything, though! And although I looked at the charts – they’re maps that show how deep the water is, plus where rocks are – my parents dealt with them.
Were there any storms?

Well, one night there was a huge one, which went on for hours. Luckily, we weren’t out at sea. When the lightning lit up the sky, I couldn’t believe the effect on the landscape – the colours were gorgeous. Seeing all the boats being knocked about in the wind was incredible.
Did you spend time on shore?

Yes – we often stopped, and it was good to get off the boat. Before the trip, I thought I’d go running whenever we were on land but there wasn’t time. But I did get to have a nice variety of tasty things to eat, most of which I’d never even heard of before. I really enjoyed that. I was hoping to chat to people, but I needed to know more Greek!
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
